name: Musashi-Koyama
tagline: A covered shopping arcade roughly 800 m long, so the shopping gets done without an umbrella on a wet day. Otemachi is 28 minutes, direct from the Meguro Line onto the Mita Line.
summary: The Tokyu Meguro Line runs through onto the Toei Mita Line and the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line, so Otemachi is 28 minutes without a change, and Shibuya 17 minutes changing at Meguro. The Musashi-Koyama shopping street, Palm, runs about 800 m from the station under a roof, and fresh food, everyday goods and restaurants are all inside it. A shopping street where you can finish the shopping without putting up an umbrella is not common even among the residential areas of the 23 wards. On the other hand, redevelopment has put two residential towers by the station, and both the rents and who lives here have been shifting.

faces.morning: The Meguro Line is busy in the morning, though not packed the way the Toyoko or Chuo Lines are. Trains arrive from the Hiyoshi direction, so a seat at Musashi-Koyama essentially does not happen. Commuters stream past the station from seven, but the shopping street is not open yet and it is quiet.
faces.daytime: Once the arcade opens, the foot traffic jumps. Shoppers are mainly older people and parents with children, and on weekday afternoons it is only inside the arcade that is busy. One street out into the residential blocks, there are few people about.
faces.night: The shops selling goods close early, but the restaurants and izakaya stay open after that. Of the 10 whose opening hours are recorded, 3 stay open past 23:00. Owner-run places remain in the small bar street by the station, so you can eat on the way home. Places open into the small hours are few.
faces.weekend: Shoppers fill the arcade, enough that passing people takes some care. It is not a destination, so the visitors are mainly people from nearby; crowds do not travel in from across the city the way they do to Nakameguro or Koenji.

terrain.note: The station sits on a terrace 28 m above sea level, with only about 5 m of variation within 800 m. The ground falls slightly towards the valley that the culverted Tachiai River follows, but the gradient is gentle. Inside the arcade it is level, and everyday shopping rarely makes you think about slopes.

exits.name: East exit (towards Palm)
exits.character: Towards the covered shopping street and the redevelopment towers; the centre of shopping and eating. Busy, and lit at night as a result.

exits.name: West exit
exits.character: Mainly housing, and calmer than the east side. It is the way through towards Togoshi and Ebara, and rents are a little lower than on the east side.

residents: Older households who use the shopping street daily, mixed with dual-income couples who moved into the redevelopment towers. Few students. The share of long-standing households used to be high, but since the towers filled the proportion of people in their thirties and forties has risen.
housingStock: Two towers by the station, mid- and low-rise blocks around them, and timber-built flats up the slope: the rents fall into three clear bands. A fair number of older timber buildings remain, so fittings differ a great deal within the same ten-minute walk. Outside the towers, newer buildings are not plentiful.
hazards: On the national hazard map, for the flood scenario based on the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Only one of the nine points within 400 m falls inside it, and the projected depth there is under 0.5 m. This is a terrace 28 m above sea level, and the projection from river flooding is small. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
stationNote: The Meguro Line runs underground here, and it takes several minutes from the platform to street level. There is a single set of gates, so you choose between the east and west exits after coming up. The Meguro Line runs through onto both the Mita and Namboku Lines, and which train you want depends on where you are going, so get into the habit of checking the destination board in the morning.
nightWalk: The shopping street and the area by the station are lit until around 22:00 and the foot traffic does not stop. Up the slope, the residential streets have fewer lamps and fewer people. Whether your way home takes you through the bar street changes the feel of the evening considerably.
rentReason: For somewhere 28 minutes direct from Otemachi, rent is not as high as at Nakameguro or Ebisu. The reasons are that the Meguro Line does not enter the Yamanote loop, that there is no large shopping complex by the station, and that the name is not known nationally. Since the redevelopment, though, rents have kept rising and the discount is not what it was.

rentRange.note: A tower by the station and an old timber-built flat up the slope differ by nearly double, even within the same ten-minute walk of Musashi-Koyama. The average looks mid-range, but what is actually on the market clusters at the two ends.
drivers: A tower, an ordinary block, or a timber-built flat

Age and construction of the building

family: Everyday goods and food are all in the shopping street, so shopping with a child in tow is less of a chore. Rinshi-no-Mori Park is within cycling distance, and there are small parks near the station. There are slopes around the station, though, so a pushchair is harder in some directions than others. Check nursery availability and school catchment by address against Shinagawa City's own current information.
medical: Kosaikai Hospital is right by the station, about 35 m away. Within walking distance there are 11 clinics and 6 pharmacies. Larger hospitals include Showa Medical University East Hospital about 1.2 km away and Showa Medical University Hospital about 1.4 km. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.

alternatives.note: If you want calmer streets and to be nearer Shibuya, choose Nakameguro. Rent for a 1LDK is about ¥50,000 higher, though, and Musashi-Koyama is the better of the two for shopping.
alternatives.lead: rents are lower at Musashi-Koyama, but Naka-Meguro is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.

alternatives.note: For commuting towards Shinagawa and Tokyo, Oimachi is quicker. It has three lines and copes better when one stops, but Musashi-Koyama wins on how usable its shopping street is.
alternatives.lead: Oimachi is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is, but Musashi-Koyama is ahead on how easy the shopping is and quiet.

outlook: The redevelopment by the station has settled, but rebuilding plans continue nearby. Nothing suggests the shopping street itself will change quickly, yet rents have kept rising as the towers filled, and that looks set to continue for now.
goodFor: People who want to do their shopping on foot
People commuting towards Otemachi and Nihonbashi without changing

People who want shopping to be easy on a wet day

residentComment: The shopping street is what stands out. Roughly 800 m of covered arcade holds fresh food, prepared dishes and restaurants, so a wet day is no obstacle to shopping. Being this close to Meguro and Shirokanedai while keeping food costs down is down to that arcade. The drawback is the slope: going home from the station into the residential streets means climbing it every time. Since the towers went up in the redevelopment, rents have clearly risen. Search on the figures from a few years ago and nothing comes up.

neighbours.lead: Musashi-Koyama is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: 772 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Musashi-Koyama. One-room rents run about ¥5,000 lower.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Musashi-Koyama, but Fudo-Mae is ahead on how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: 1134 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 3 minutes sooner than Musashi-Koyama. One-room rents run about ¥14,000 higher.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 16 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, very few of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyu Meguro Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.exits: The covered shopping street at the east exit is the centre of shopping and eating; the west exit is mainly housing, and rents there are a little lower.
leads.noiseSources: 鮫洲大山線 runs 156 m away, so whether a flat faces it changes what you hear indoors.
